title: Immersion Accelerator: 21-Day Personalized Onboarding Pilot
body:
Executive summary:
A lightweight experiment to personalize the first 21 calendar days of new IC onboarding. The bundle pairs a short day-0 micro-survey, an explicit mentor-match with reason, and a one-page skills-gap playbook focused on three high-impact actions. Goal: reduce time-to-first-meaningful-contribution (TTFMC), improve early hire sentiment, and surface repeatable playbooks for common gap profiles.

Problem statement:
Current onboarding is consistent but high-variance. Some hires ramp quickly; others spend their first weeks discovering what to learn. Managers and mentors spend time triaging unknown gaps instead of enabling ship-focused work. Small, targeted personalization should be low-friction and reducible to templates.

Success metrics (pilot):
- Primary: reduce median TTFMC by ~20% for pilot cohort vs recent baseline (TTFMC measured by first merged PR or first completed shipped task).
- Secondary: +0.5 average weekly sentiment (5-point scale) by day 21; reduce manager ramp-uncertainty by 30% (survey); fewer unresolved access/tooling blockers >48h.

Scope and constraints:
- Pilot size: up to 15 hires across engineering, product, and SRE over 8 weeks (rolling start).
- No changes to access/security processes.
- Mentor load capped at two active new hires during pilot.

Core components:
1) Day-0 micro-survey (5 items): recent role summary (1-2 bullets), confidence ratings on: codebase/infra/CI/debugging/support, preferred learning style (docs/demo/pair), two top 21-day learning goals, mentoring cadence preference, timezone/PTO flags.
2) Mentor match with explicit reason: post assignment to #onboard-match using a short template describing which gaps the mentor will focus on. Primary mentor focuses on product/domain unblock; secondary mentor supports tooling/infra if needed.
3) One-page skills-gap playbook: three focused actions with time estimates and expected deliverable (e.g., read X doc, pair on small fix, ship doc or minor change).

Operational runbook (high level):
- Day -1: send micro-survey and request hiring manager endorsement.
- Day 0-3: mentor kickoff, access validation, assign a first tiny shipable task.
- Day 4-10: execute playbook; collect daily one-line standups from hire.
- Day 11-21: push toward first merged PR / shipped task; capture sentiment, mentor notes, and final checklist.

Data collection & signals:
- Quantitative: time-to-first-merged-PR (repo events), weekly sentiment scores (short Google Form), count of unresolved blockers >48h.
- Qualitative: mentor notes at day 7/14/21 (three bullets), hire free-text feedback at week 1 and week 3, manager check-in notes.

Escalation rules:
- No merged PR or shipped task by day 14 without explicit remediation plan -> escalate to manager + People Ops.
- Two consecutive sentiment scores <= 2 -> same-day People Ops + manager 1:1.
- Access issues unresolved >48 hours -> infra ops SLA tagging and intervention.

Playbook examples (copyable templates):
- Repo Familiarity (Novice): 1) Read top-level README + CONTRIBUTING.md + two high-level docs (30-60m). 2) Pair with mentor on a small cleanup or test (2-3h). 3) Submit a doc update or minor fix and request review (1-2h).
- CI & Debugging (Basic): 1) Run unit tests locally; capture failures (1-2h). 2) Shadow a deploy with infra mentor (1-2h). 3) Triage a flaky test or reproduce a failure and file a short PR or issue (2-4h).
- Customer Support Readiness (Low->Medium): 1) Read support runbook and top 10 customer cases (1-2h). 2) Shadow a Tier 1 triage rotation (2-3h). 3) Create a short cheat-sheet for common triage steps (1h).

Mentor guidance (short):
- Set clear first-session outcomes: validate access, agree a first tiny task, define one 7-day learning goal.
- Use the micro-playbook to surface blockers; keep notes brief.
- Respect the two-mentee cap during the pilot and log time spent for later recognition.

Manager check-in scripts (concise):
- Week 1 (15 minutes): Are there blockers? Missing access? What should we pause to create focus? Preferred mentoring cadence?
- Week 2 (20-30 minutes): Status on two 21-day goals? Any surprises about role scope? Adjust mentoring or task scope as needed.

Hypotheses to validate:
- H1: Micro-survey will surface >=70% of actionable gaps mentors would otherwise discover by day 7.
- H2: Mentor matching by gap-vector accelerates median TTFMC vs random assignment.
- H3: Short, prioritized playbooks increase sentiment and reduce early blocking incidents.

Risks & mitigations:
- Mentor overload: cap mentees and recruit mix of senior+mid mentors; provide public recognition.
- Noisy metrics due to role heterogeneity: normalize TTFMC by role cohort and use relative improvement.
- Low survey completion: keep survey <2 minutes and manager endorses completion pre-boarding.

Pilot timeline:
- Week 0: finalize survey wording and playbook templates; recruit mentors.
- Weeks 1-8: rolling pilot with up to 2 hires/week.
- Week 9: analysis (quantitative + qualitative) and decision: adopt, iterate, or sunset.

Ownership & immediate action items:
- Owner: Nina Park (People Ops).
- Eng onboarding lead: Michael Grant -> recruit mentors and validate first-task templates.
- Action items: finalize form by 2026-02-18; recruit mentors by 2026-02-24; confirm first-task templates for pilot roles by 2026-02-26.

Privacy & storage:
- Survey responses stored in People Ops Drive with restricted access. Remind hires not to paste customer PII in free-text fields.

Notes & friction log (quick):
- Keep playbooks extremely short; long reading reduces adoption.
- Prefer one-line daily standups to minimize reporting burden.
- Track mentor time for later compensation or recognition.

Document status history:
- Created 2026-02-14 by Nina Park.
- Iteration notes: 2026-02-18 updated survey flow; 2026-02-20 clarified escalation rules and added CI playbook.
